basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A collective of two or more actors working under a shared mandate, not a legal organization or a position.
Membership is a set of time-bounded assignment facts, so past composition stays visible.
Differs from an identity-provider group, which grants access, and from a cohort list, which only collects members.
A team is not a project, though it may be assigned to one.

may: Record a team, its mandate and its membership assignments from authoritative sources.
Answer who is on a team at a given time.
Notify team owners of expired or overlapping assignments.
Join a team as a non-human member where its mandate permits.
mustNot: Add or remove members without the team owner's decision.
Use team membership as an access grant without the access system.
Infer individual performance from team metrics.
requiresHuman: Creating or dissolving a team with a formal mandate.
Removing a member for conduct reasons.

considerations: Membership records show who worked with whom and can be used for profiling.
Non-human members should be identified as such to other team members.
Team outcomes should not be blamed on individuals without fair process.
affectedParties: Managers who form and dissolve teams

items: A team has a name, a mandate, an owning unit and membership assignments with start and end dates.
It is confused with a department, an access group and a project.
Access granted to former members through stale membership.
Unclear responsibility when membership is not current.
Profiling of individuals through collaboration patterns.
